title: Who is a Hindu?
byline: by Koenraad Elst · Voice of India · 2001 · subtitled Hindu Revivalist Views of Animism, Buddhism, Sikhism and Other Offshoots of Hinduism
lede: There is no agreed definition of “Hindu”, and Elst argues the vagueness has political consequences. Groups that call themselves non-Hindu can claim minority rights, such as running their own schools under Article 30 of the Constitution. He tests the competing definitions (by belief, by history, by law, and by Savarkar's Hindutva) against the hard cases: tribals, Jains, Sikhs, Buddhists, Ambedkarite neo-Buddhists, the Arya Samaj and the Ramakrishna Mission. He concludes in favour of a historical definition: Hinduism is all of Indian paganism.
facts: groups examined: reformists, Jains, Sikhs, tribals, Buddhists, neo-Buddhists, travelling gurus
the Ramakrishna Mission declared non-Hindu by the Calcutta High Court, then ruled Hindu by the Supreme Court
Savarkar's Hindutva published, its definition written in prison
note: Who counts as Hindu is contested, and many Sikhs, Jains, Buddhists and Ambedkarites reject being included. This page summarises Elst's analysis and conclusion, attributed to him.

sections.title: Are they Hindus?
items: Argued in court that “Ramakrishnaism” was a separate religion, to protect its schools. The Supreme Court ruled on 2 July 1995 that it was not.
The Arya Samaj and travelling gurus
Reformist and exported Hinduism, still Hindu in Elst's view.
Sought minority status. Elst reviews Dayananda's critique and the claim that Hindus destroyed Jain temples.
Elst argues “Sikhs were Hindus”, and that a separate identity was promoted under British rule.
Animists and nature-worshippers, Hindu by the historical definition.
From Dayananda's critique to Vivekananda's and Coomaraswamy's embrace, and Savarkar's charge of “defeatism”. Ambedkar's 1956 conversion.

sections.title: What Elst recommends
items: Accept that in everyday speech “Hindu” is narrower.
By that test, the inclusive usage of Hindu activists is “100% correct”.
Hindus should claim the Buddha, Mahavira and the Sikh Gurus as their own, without coercion.
